summary: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages.
takeaways: Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures.
We present LLM-Attacker, a framework that records these choices and lets researchers check, compare and extend an evaluation.
This experiment is shared with a companion study; here, it tests how the evaluation responds to a change in attacker access.
